title: Wärtsilä to supply 282 MW onsite power solution for a U.S. data center as AI growth intensifies demand for reliable power
source_used: Wärtsilä press release on wartsila.com (pool link, fetched text); this is the company's own announcement
key_facts: Wärtsilä announced on 5 Oct 2026 an order to supply a 282-megawatt onsite power solution for a data center project being developed by a major US independent power producer, which it does not name.
The power plant will operate with 15 Wärtsilä 50SG engines.
The order was booked in the third quarter of 2026 and is Wärtsilä's seventh data center order in the US, bringing its US data center power sales to more than 3 gigawatts.
Equipment delivery is scheduled for 2028, and the project is expected to be fully operational in 2029.
Wärtsilä says grid constraints, lengthy connection timelines and rising AI electricity demand create power availability problems for new data centers.
The customer chose the engine-based solution for large-scale capacity on efficient timelines, with room to expand in phases.
Wärtsilä says the engines use a closed-loop cooling system that cuts water use compared with conventional thermal power and can be converted to future fuels (company claims).
quote_evidence: Technology group Wärtsilä has secured an order to supply a 282 MW onsite power solution for a data center project being developed by a major US independent power producer in the United States.
The Wärtsilä equipment is scheduled for delivery in 2028, and the project is expected to become fully operational in 2029.
It marks the company's seventh data center-related order in the United States, bringing the total power capacity sold by Wärtsilä for U.S. data center applications to more than 3 GW.
why_it_matters_hint: Developers of AI data centers are ordering their own on-site power plants because grid connections are slow, according to the company that sells them.
event_date: Announced 5 Oct 2026; order booked in Q3 2026.
notes: Company press release; the customer, site and price are not named. The engines, water and fuel claims are Wärtsilä's own.
